Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has tweaked the underside of the RB 19 by moving the small “floor fences” and adding a slightly more angled section to the floor edge. The new placement smooths the airflow under the car, giving a bite of extra down‑force, while the locally increased camber helps the car stick better through the corners. Together these changes should boost cornering stability and tyre life, giving the team a sharper edge on the opening weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has tweaked the rear wing’s camber – basically angling the flap a bit differently – to match the specific load demands of this circuit. The change should give the car a more stable rear end and a little extra bite in the corners, helping the drivers extract more speed and confidence over the weekend’s layout.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin has trimmed the aggressiveness of its front and rear wings – the front wing now has a milder flap, while the rear wing’s front‑view area is smaller – and swapped in a single‑element beam wing to cut drag. The net effect is a cleaner, lower‑drag aero package that should boost straight‑line speed and make the car more balanced on this circuit’s mix of corners and long straights, giving the team a better chance to fight at the front of the grid this weekend.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has tweaked the front of the car – a new brake‑duct shape sharpens the airflow over the front wheels, keeping the brakes cooler and feeding more front‑end grip. At the same time, the front suspension geometry has been re‑profiled to give the car a smoother, more stable feel through the corners, meaning drivers can push harder and keep the tyres in their sweet spot for this weekend’s race.

Williams Racing: Williams is trialling a fresh, shorter‑chord beam wing this weekend – a plug‑in part that’s slimmer than the one they used last year. By trimming the wing’s surface it cuts drag, giving the car a boost on the straights without sacrificing the down‑force they need in the corners. If the package works, it could translate into better qualifying laps and more competitive race pace on a circuit that rewards top‑end speed.
Sauber / Audi: Sauber‑Audi has reshaped the cover over the front suspension, tweaking the airflow around the front wheels. The new shape smooths the air coming off the front end, which helps the car stick to the track a bit better and gives drivers a more stable, responsive feel through corners. In short, it’s a small aerodynamic tweak that could translate into a few extra tenths on the lap times this weekend.
